Collaborate API Reference

api-overview > collaborate-api-reference

Organizations worldwide face increasingly sophisticated and coordinated cybersecurity threats, making it crucial for security teams to adopt a collaborative approach to define their security strategy. Collaborate is a situational awareness platform that enables real-time threat alert sharing and aggregation, helping you effectively respond to threats through information sharing, coordination, and collaboration among security analysts. With Collaborate, you can enrich, anonymize, and share precise threat intelligence, including indicators of compromise (IOCs) and incident responses. Collaborate's API is organized around REST and is available to all customers. The API endpoints contain predictable resource-oriented URLs, return JSON-encoded responses, and use standard HTTP response codes and authentication.

For AI agents and LLM-based discovery, see the [Collaborate LLM-friendly API Guide](https://csapapi.cyware.com/collaborate-api-reference/llms.txt).

In Collaborate's Analyst Portal, you can manage user access and feature permissions by defining Open API roles and generating credentials to control access.

### Create Open API Roles

You can create user roles for members to regulate access to Collaborate features using open API. You can assign these roles to members while generating API credentials for them. For more information, see [Create Open API Roles](https://techdocs.cyware.com/csap/en/configure-collaborate-open-api.html##).

You can generate open API credentials for analysts or members to access the open API endpoints. You can assign a role to control and restrict members' access to Collaborate's features. chunks.title: Create Alert
chunks.text:
Create Alert analyst-portal > analyst-portal-alerts > create-alert POST csap/v1/create_card Create an alert on the Collaborate Analyst Portal and publish it to the intended recipients. You can also add custom fields while creating an alert. The format to include custom fields is described in the custom field structures. ### Changelog Supports scheduling alert expiry using scheduled_expiry_time parameter. Added support for the share_with, reference_urls, and pirs body parameters. Access to certain categories is based on your user role in the Analyst Portal. This update does not impact credentials generated prior to this version. ### Alert Field Types As an analyst, you can create alerts using custom fields tailored to your needs. Use fields like text boxes for detailed input, multi-select for tagging multiple values, single-select for predefined choices, and more to customize your alerts effectively. For details on retrieving additional field information, see the Retrieve Additional Fields section. Use the table below for custom field format: Field Type Description Format Boolean Boolean fields allow you to select either true or false for specific options. While creating an alert, you can use these fields to indicate details such as whether the alert is Publicly Shareable or Requires Immediate Action. field_id: value Example: "f65b26a174658": true Text Text boxes allow you to add information in text format. While creating an alert, you can use these fields to provide details such as Threat Description, Likely Motivation, and more. field_id: Text Example: "f533606babb44": "CVE-2014-12345" Single-select Single-select fields allow you to choose one option from a predefined list. These fields are used to capture key details of an alert, such as Threat Level or Severity. field_id: { field_id_id: selected value id} Example: "ffa80c88f1d20": { "ffa80c88f1d20_id": "oaa822c36c133" } Multi-select Multi-select fields allow you to associate multiple options with an alert from a predefined list. For example, you can use these fields to assign Affected Sectors or Indicators. field_id: [{ field_id_id: selected value id}, { field_id_id: selected value id}] Example: "f65b26a174658": [ { "f65b26a174658_id": "o15f317d51bec" }, { "f65b26a174658_id": "o43d57e02d92a" } ] Date & Time Date and time fields let you capture time-sensitive details for an alert, such as Reported At or Action Deadline. The values are stored in Epoch (Unix timestamp) format. field_id: Epoch value Example: "f9c217dfe8824": 1709725603 Additional fields are system or custom fields that you can use while creating alerts. To ensure accurate field mapping, you need to retrieve the field IDs and details before passing them as body parameters. To retrieve field details, follow these steps: 1. Use the **Get Additional Fields List** endpoint in the Alerts section to retrieve the list of all fields, including their field IDs. 2. Use the `field_id` in the **Get Additional Fields Details** endpoint to retrieve associated field details. Body fields: - title (required, string): Pass the title of the alert. Example: *New Malware Variant Targeting Enterprise Networks* - content (required, string): Pass the description of the alert. - is_content_defanged (optional, boolean): Pass true to specify that the link is not clickable. - card_image (optional, string): Pass the URL for the alert image. Ensure that the value is a valid URL. Example: *https://cyware.com/cyware.jpg.* To pass this field, ensure the `type` field is also included. - type (optional, string): Pass the type of the alert image. The current supported type is *URL*. - card_info (optional, string): Pass any additional details for the alert. Note: You can use HTML format for the additional information.
Example: Adversary:,
Malware Families: njRAT, AsyncRAT, Houdini RAT
Attack IDs: T1104, T1547", - card_category (optional, object): Pass the category for the alert. Example: { "category_id": "154c4d4c", "category_name": "Malware Advisory"}
Use the **Get Category List** endpoint to retrieve the list of alert categories. To assign a category to the alert, pass either the `card_category` or `card_category_name` parameter. `card_category` takes precedence if both are passed. - card_category_name (optional, string): Pass the alert category associated with your user role in the Analyst Portal. Example: *Malware*.
To assign a category, pass either the `card_category` or `card_category_name` parameters.
Note: `card_category` takes precedence if both are passed. - card_group (optional, array): Pass the list of recipient group IDs for the alert publication. You can retrieve the list of available recipient groups using the **Get Recipient Groups** endpoint. `group_id` is a required key for the recipient group.
Note: This is a required field if status is PUBLISHED. - pirs (optional, array): Pass one or more comma-separated IDs of published Intelligence Requirements (IRs) to associate with the alert for enrichment. You can retrieve a list of IRs using the *Get IRs* endpoint. - reference_urls (optional, array): Pass one or more comma-separated URLs to offer additional context or information related to the alert. - defang_ioc_in_ioc_attachments (optional, boolean): Pass true to defang the IOCs in the attachment. - threat_indicators_obj (optional, object): Pass the threat indicators associated with the alert. - push_email_notification (optional, boolean): Pass true to send email notifications to the recipients. - push_required (optional, boolean): Pass true to send mobile notifications to the recipients. - card_organization (optional, array): Pass the list of organizations for the alert publication. You can retrieve the available organization types using the **Get Organizations** endpoint. The `organization_type_id` is a required key for each organization type. - tags (optional, array): Pass the list of tags associated with the alert. Example: *["malware", "vulnerability"]*. - custom_fields (optional, object): Pass the custom fields linked to the alert. chunks.title: Get Alerts
chunks.text:
Get Alerts

analyst-portal > analyst-portal-alerts > alerts-list-analyst-member

GET csap/v1/list_alert/

Returns a list of alerts from Collaborate.

### Changelog


Added support for the channel_ids query parameter.
For analysts, access to alerts is determined by the categories associated with your user role in the Analyst Portal. However, if your user role has View All Alerts permission, you can access all alerts based on your preference. This update does not impact credentials generated prior to this version.

Query parameters:
- status (optional, string): Pass the status of the alerts to be retrieved. Published alerts are retrieved based on the published time in epoch format. Expired and drafted alerts are retrieved based on the modified time for the alert.
- start_time (optional, string): Pass the start date of the query in epoch format. This represents the earliest timestamp for any alert in the query. Example: *1737405600*
- end_time (optional, string): Pass the end date of the query in epoch format. This represents the latest timestamp for any alert in the query. Example: *1737441600*
- page_size (optional, number): Pass the number of records on a page. Example: *10*
- page (optional, number): Pass the page number for the response. Example: *2*
- category_id (optional, string): Pass the category ID to filter alerts. Enter multiple category IDs separated by a comma. You can retrieve `category_id` using the **Get Category List** endpoint. Example: *4bfd32c0,c7012fcc*
- tlp (optional, string): Pass the TLP to filter alerts. Enter multiple TLPs separated by a comma. Example: *GREEN*
- title (optional, string): Pass the title to filter alerts. Example: *Ransomware Attacks are on the Rise*
- channel_ids (optional, string): Pass the channel IDs to filter alerts. You can enter multiple channel IDs separated by a comma.

chunks.text:
Organization

Organizations can also be further grouped into organization types and be associated with certain organizational levels. This allows analysts to share alerts quickly with members from selected organizations and organization types. For more information, see [Collaborate Organization Documentation](https://techdocs.cyware.com/csap/en/member-organization.html).

As an analyst, you can perform the following actions:

*   **Create and Manage Organizations**: Create organizations, assign them to members, and update organization details for seamless alert sharing.
    
*   **Activate or Deactivate Organizations**: Enable or disable organizations as needed to align with operational requirements.
    
*   **Retrieve Organization Data**: Access detailed lists of organizations, organization types, and organization levels in Collaborate.
    
*   **Retrieve Associated Details**: Obtain domains and IP addresses linked to a specific organization.

With the features provided by the Member Portal, members can stay updated with crucial information and prepare for the potential impact of cyber events and other developments.

As an analyst, you can add Collaborate members as well as modify and manage members, including setting their status to inactive. For more information, see [Collaborate Member Documentation](https://techdocs.cyware.com/csap/en/onboard-members.html).

Add Member analyst-portal > member > add-member POST csap/v1/create_end_user/ Add a member user to Collaborate's Member Portal. > [!NOTE] > * It is advised not to add a member if mandatory custom fields are enabled. > * To enable Intel Lake for a member through the features body parameter, ensure that you have a valid license. For more information, see [Collaborate documentation](https://techdocs.cyware.com/en/299669-308321-add-members.html#299669-308321-add-members). ### Changelog Added support for the features body parameter Added support for the member_roles body parameter Body fields: - email (required, string): Pass the email address of the member user you want to add. - first_name (required, string): Pass the name of the member. - organization_type (required, object): Pass the organization type. You can retrieve the list of organization types using the **Get Organization Types** endpoint.
Example, *"organization_type": { "org_type_id": "a95f3553-ea8e-4f95-8e6a-43d47997c50c", "org_type_name": "Media and Communications" }.* - organization (required, object): Pass the organization that the member belongs to. You can retrieve the list of organizations using the **Get Organizations** endpoint.
Example, *"organization": { "organization_id": "3cf257a6-e329-48b7-8c14-815d3c358bae", "organization_name": "Example Org"}*. - member_roles (optional, array): Pass the member role to assign it to the member. - user_group (optional, array): Pass the group ID of the recipient group the member is part of. chunks.title: Upload File
chunks.text:
Upload File analyst-portal > analyst-portal-doc-library > upload-file POST csap/v1/upload_media/ Upload a file to the Doc Library and share it with recipient groups and individual recipients. ### Changelog * Added support for the `parent_folder_id` body parameter * The API response now includes the `parent_folder_id` field Body fields: - user_groups (required, text): Pass the group IDs of the recipient groups you want to share this file with. Enter multiple recipient groups using comma as a separator. Get a list of all recipient groups using the **Get Recipient Groups** endpoint. - tlp (optional, text): Pass the TLP associated with the media. - file (required, file): Specify the file path or select the file from your local system to upload to the Doc Library.
If the parameter `file_name` is not passed, then the default file name is `uuid-uploaded_file_name.file_format`. Here, `uploaded_file_name` refers to the name of the file saved on your local system.
Example: *694892c5-Sample_file.png* - individual_recipients (required, text): Pass the email IDs of the individual recipients that you want to share this file with. Enter multiple email addresses using comma as a separator. Example: *john.doe@example.com*. Note: You can pass either `user_groups` or `individual_recipients` while uploading media. - file_name (optional, text): Pass the name of the file with which the file is saved in Doc Library.
Example: Test Image Default format is `uuid-uploaded_file_name.file_format` - parent_folder_id (optional, string): Pass the ID of the parent folder where you want to upload the file. If you do not pass this ID, the file will be uploaded to the root directory. To retrieve the parent ID, use the **Get Folder Details** endpoint.

Create Folder analyst-portal > analyst-portal-doc-library > create-folder POST csap/v1/folder-details/ Creates a new folder in the Doc Library within the specified parent folder. If you do not specify any parent folder, the new folder is created in the root directory. ### Changelog This endpoint is available starting from the 3.8.5.0 version. Body fields: - folder_name (required, string): Pass the name of the folder in 100 characters. - description (optional, string): Pass a brief description of the folder in 500 characters. - recipient_groups (optional, array): Pass the recipient groups who can access this folder.
If you pass the `parent_folder_id`, ensure to include the recipient groups that have permission to access the parent folder while creating this folder. If the parent folder does not include any recipient groups, you can assign any recipient groups to the child folder. To retrieve the list of recipient groups for the parent folder, use the **Get Folder Details** endpoint. - individual_recipients (optional, array): Pass the individual recipients who can access this folder.
If you pass the `parent_folder_id`, ensure to include the individual recipients that are part of the parent folder while creating this folder. To retrieve the list of individual recipients for the parent folder, use the **Get Folder Details** endpoint - parent_folder_id (optional, string): Pass the ID of the parent folder to create this folder in it. By default, the folder is created in the root directory. You can retrieve the `parent_folder_id` using the **Get Folder Details** endpoint.

- alert_id (required, string): Pass the ID of the alert associated with the recommended action. To retrieve the alert ID, use the **Get Alerts** endpoint.

chunks.title: Create Intel
chunks.text:
Create Intel

member-portal > member-portal-intel > create-intel

POST csap/v1/report_intel/

As a member, you can submit threat intel to analysts.


The required fields while submitting intel is based on the configuration for the intel category in the Analyst Portal. To get the required fields for the category, follow these steps:
1.  Use the **Get Intel Categories **API in the Intel section to retrieve the list of all categories. You can use the `category_id` of the category to retrieve all associated fields.
2.  Use this `category_id` in the **Get** **Intel** **Category Details** API to fetch all the fields associated with the category. All fields marked as required true are mandatory while submitting the RFI.
While passing body parameters, the field ID is mandatory. To retrieve field details, follow these steps:
1.  Use the **Get Additional Fields** API in the Alerts section to retrieve the list of all fields. You can use the `field_id` to retrieve all associated details.
2.  Use this field_id in **Get Additional Field Details** to fetch all the field details. The ID of the field is a required key while submitting RFIs. For example, for the Priority field, the `priority_id` is a required key.
As a member, you can submit intel using custom fields tailored to your needs. Use fields like text boxes for detailed input, multi-select for tagging multiple values, single-select for predefined choices, and more to customize your intel effectively.
Field Type
Description
Format
Boolean
Boolean fields allow you to select either true or false for specific options.
field_id: value Example: "f65b26a174658": true
Text
Text boxes allow you to add information in text format.
field_id: Text Example: "f533606babb44": "CVE-2014-12345"
Single-select
Single-select fields allow you to choose one option from a predefined list.
field_id: { field_id_id: selected value id} Example: "ffa80c88f1d20": { "ffa80c88f1d20_id": "oaa822c36c133" }
Multi-select
Multi-select fields allow you to associate multiple options from a predefined list.
field_id: [{ field_id_id: selected value id}, { field_id_id: selected value id}] Example: "f65b26a174658": [ { "f65b26a174658_id": "o15f317d51bec" }, { "f65b26a174658_id": "o43d57e02d92a" } ]

Body fields:
- category (required, string): Pass the category of intel. You can use the **Get Intel Categories** endpoint to fetch the `category_id`. You can then use this ID to get the required fields associated with the category using the **Get Intel Category Details** endpoint. Note: `category_id` is a required key for this field.
- title (required, string): Pass the title of the intel.
- description (required, string): Pass the description for the intel.
- tlp (required, string): Pass the TLP associated with the intel.
- priority (optional, object): Pass the priority of details associated with the intel. Use the **Get Additional Fields** endpoint to fetch the `field_id`. You can use the `field_id` to fetch details for this field using the **Get Additional Fields Details** endpoint.
- optional_fields (optional, object): Pass the optional fields associated with the RFI.
- user_group (required, array): Pass the details of one or more user groups to which you want to submit the intel. This field is required only if direct submission is enabled for you. Depending on the settings in the Analyst Portal, you can either pass `user_groups` or organizations.

As a member, you can submit an RFI using custom fields tailored to your needs. Use fields like text boxes for detailed input, multi-select for tagging multiple values, single-select for predefined choices, and more to customize your RFI effectively.

Description
Format

- recipient_type (required, string): Pass the recipient type for the recommended action. This determines the default group of users who will receive the action.
- assigned_to (optional, array): Pass a comma-separated list of one or more email IDs of the users to whom the recommended action is assigned. You can only assign users who are recipients of the associated alert. To retrieve the list of individual recipient email IDs for the alert, use the **Get Alert Details** endpoint.
- assigned_groups (optional, array): Pass a comma-separated list of one or more IDs of recipient groups to whom the recommended action is assigned. You can only assign groups that are recipients of the associated alert. To retrieve the list of recipient groups for the alert, use the **Get Alert Details** endpoint.
- due_date (optional, integer): Pass the due date for the recommended action in epoch format.
- alert_id (required, string): Pass the ID of the alert associated with the recommended action. To retrieve the alert ID, use the **Get Alerts** endpoint.
